value: Light availability modulated flowering after crown loss in the two studied palms; palms beneath more complete canopies flowered less
method: abstract report of long-term field monitoring plus crown-clipping and fertilization experiments
conditions: Serenoa repens and Sabal etonia across four Florida vegetative associations;9900 plant-year records pooled across the study

source.title: EPISODIC REPRODUCTION IN TWO FIRE‐PRONE PALMS, SERENOA REPENS AND SABAL ETONIA (PALMAE)

where: EuropePMC AGR abstract, original study; full paper unread
quote: The loss of a palm’s crown by fire, or by clipping, stimulated flowering, but this effect was mediated by light availability.
note: Abstract-only report covering two named palm species; no species-separated treatment estimate, light threshold or photoreceptor identified. Full paper remains wanted. Clipping is an intervention but canopy light comparison is observational; light-mediated flowering is not evidence of eyes, an endogenous daily rhythm, or a measured receptor mechanism.
